metadata.title: The nopunt Skill
metadata.audience: Brutalist fellows already using Claude Code
metadata.note: Skill teardown of skills/make/nopunt/SKILL.md (episode.source_sha256 db5dbdc4…). The nopunt skill is the anti-punt catalog — the single place a Brutalist author checks before dropping ANY placeholder in a beat sheet. It answers 'can I draw this, and how?' with one triage: HOLD is only a genuine archival PHOTOGRAPH; everything else in the catalog animates, so leaving it unfilled is a PUNT (a bug, not a style choice). Step zero routes every beat through the library first (./art scenes). The catalog maps narration-shape → animation form → tool: Manim owns morphing math/geometry, Remotion owns composed cards / typography / UI, the app skin (ClaudeCodeBeat / composer / shell / GitHub) shows the REAL artifact, FormB cards list 2–5 named things with icons, FormA is the last-resort word card. A permanent block-list of 'punt costumes' names the same bug in different hats: gen-AI clip, unfilled fill_slates slate, a card whose narration names a visual, DoodleScene / DoodleChart, STILL src=archive for a concept. And SHOW/HOLD/CARD is the per-beat vocabulary — anything else is a PUNT. Voice: Kokoro am_onyx — Liam in for Bear (IN-FOR-BEAR LAW). Outro is ClaudeTitleOutro (hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK); inner composer folder chip is @HumanitariansAI per playlist. Live demo captured in demo/nopunt-run.log — three real `./art scenes` invocations (search, --check hit, --check banned-costume, --check miss).

beats.narration_text: The easy read is that nopunt is a linter — a rejection tool that flags bad placeholders. It is not. The nopunt skill is a catalog. A routing table you check before you fill a beat. It maps narration shape to a real component, and it refuses the punt costumes that keep sneaking back in. Only a genuine archival photograph is a legitimate hold. Everything else, the catalog animates.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK-FIRST — the anatomy of nopunt: the SKILL.md file itself, the catalog rows, the SHOW/HOLD/CARD vocabulary, the block-list, and the sibling skills that read it.
beats.narration_text: First, the anatomy. Nopunt is one file — SKILL dot md — and it does five jobs. It defines the HOLD versus PUNT rule. It publishes the catalog — a table of narration shape mapped to animation form and to the tool that renders it. It fixes the SHOW slash HOLD slash CARD vocabulary that every authoring loop reads. It names the punt costumes to reject on sight — the same bug in different hats. And it stays synced with the actual scene registry, so the lint has one source of truth. Sibling skills — ai dash explainer, deep dash explainer, cli dash explainer — do not repeat these rules. They reference this file.

beats.role_note: The pipeline — how a beat gets routed. Step zero is `./art scenes`, then tool choice, then SHOW/HOLD/CARD classification. If nothing fits, that is a design card, not a slate.
beats.narration_text: The pipeline. Every beat goes through five gates, and only the first is optional if you already know your component. Step zero — ask the library. Run art scenes with what the beat needs in plain words, and art scenes dash dash check the name it suggests. If the library has it, use it. Then route by narration shape. Moving mechanism, math, geometry — Manim. Composed card, typography, UI — Remotion. Real code, real terminal, real diff — the app skin. A short list of named things — FormB. Words with nothing to show — FormA. Then classify — SHOW, HOLD, or CARD. Anything else — including a genuine miss — becomes a design card. The catalog logs the miss to TEMPLATE dash MISSES dot md automatically. A miss is never a licence to slate.

beats.role_note: Design decision 1 — HOLD vs PUNT. Only a real archival photograph is a HOLD. Everything else animates, so unfilled is a PUNT (a bug, not a style choice).
beats.narration_text: First design decision, and it is the whole rule. HOLD versus PUNT. HOLD means the beat needs a genuine archival photograph — a real person, a real place, a real document, a real event — or a judgment only Bear can make. That is the only legitimate placeholder. Everything else is a PUNT. A slot the system could draw itself but deferred. Every row in the catalog below is animatable. So if a beat's content appears in the catalog and is left unfilled, that is a bug — not a design choice, not a stylistic hold, not a taste question. Author it.

beats.role_note: Design decision 2 — THE CATALOG. Narration shape → animation form → tool. Six families cover everything animatable.
beats.narration_text: Second decision. The catalog. Every beat's narration has a shape, and the catalog maps that shape to a form and to the tool that renders it. Six families. Data and quantity — bars, stat cards, donuts, itemized lists. Structure and relationship — grids, funnels, flow diagrams, stacks, gates. Math and mechanism — equations built term by term, geometric transforms. Enumerated concepts — FormB cards, one icon per named thing. Code and app and interface — the real artifact, in the real skin. And text bookends — FormA and the four fixed beats. If a beat's content lands in any of these families, the tool is already picked. The author's job is just to route it.

beats.role_note: Design decision 3 — PUNT COSTUMES. The block-list. Same bug in different hats. None is ever a valid fill for animatable content.
beats.narration_text: Third decision. The block-list. Nopunt names five punt costumes — the same bug in different hats — and none of them is ever a valid fill for animatable content. One — YOU dropping in a gen dash AI clip. Two — an unfilled fill underscore slates or remotion underscore scenes slate left in the master. Three — a FormA card whose narration names a visual, like the routing diagram or a funnel. Four — DoodleScene or DoodleChart, permanently cut from this register. Five — STILL source archive, drop a historical image, for a concept or a dataset. Each of these maps to a row in the catalog above. Draw it.

props.heading: Five costumes. One bug.
props.body: The five punt costumes nopunt bans on sight: (1) a gen-AI clip / pantry still filling a concept slot; (2) an unfilled fill_slates or remotion_scenes slate in the master; (3) a FormA card whose narration NAMES a visual ("the routing diagram", "a funnel"); (4) DoodleScene / DoodleChart — permanently cut; (5) STILL src=archive standing in for a concept or dataset. Each maps to a catalog row. Author the row.

beats.role_note: Design decision 4 — SHOW/HOLD/CARD is the per-beat vocabulary. Every authoring loop uses it. Anything else is a PUNT.
beats.narration_text: Fourth decision, and it is the vocabulary every authoring loop reads. SHOW, HOLD, or CARD. SHOW — a real skin surface, a Manim diagram, a Remotion scene, or a legible artifact renders the beat's content, and its component is named in the shot block. HOLD — a real archival photograph, or a judgment only Bear can make, with a one dash line hold underscore reason next to it. CARD — a few words with nothing to show, an act divider or an aphorism, last resort. If a card's narration names a visual or makes a factual claim, that is a PUNT, not a card. Anything outside these three is a PUNT — a bug, not a style choice.

props.heading: SHOW · HOLD · CARD.
props.body: SHOW — a real skin surface, Manim diagram, Remotion scene, or legible artifact renders the beat; component/scene ID is named in shot. HOLD — genuine archival photograph or a creator-only judgment; requires a one-line hold_reason. CARD — a few words with nothing to show (act divider, aphorism, breathing beat); last resort. A card whose narration names a visual or asserts a fact is a PUNT, not a card. Anything else is a PUNT.
props.quote: SHOW / HOLD / CARD — the per-beat classification. Anything else is a PUNT — a bug, not a style choice.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — when the catalog GENUINELY misses. That is a scripting gap to FLAG (a design card), not a licence to slate.
beats.narration_text: Falsifiability. What if the catalog does not fit. It happens. A concept lands that has no row — nothing moves, no listable set, no code artifact, no real photo. Nopunt is explicit about this case. It is a scripting gap to FLAG — never a gen dash AI clip, never an archive still, never a card of words dressed up as a beat. The search writes the miss to TEMPLATE dash MISSES dot md by itself, with dash dash reel pointing at the reel that needed it, and the next author sees the ask. A miss is a design task. Build the component and the next reel finds it forever. But a miss is never a licence to slate.

body: catalog gap → TEMPLATE-MISSES.md · not a slate
quote block lands verbatim from SKILL.md

props.heading: A miss is a design card.
props.body: When nothing in the catalog genuinely fits, that is a scripting gap to FLAG — never a gen-AI clip, never an archive still, never a card of words. The `./art scenes` search logs the miss to TEMPLATE-MISSES.md by itself, tagged with the reel path via --reel. Build the component and the next reel finds it forever. But a miss is never a licence to slate.
props.quote: Only when the library genuinely has nothing does the tool choice below apply, and that miss is a design card: the search writes it to TEMPLATE-MISSES.md itself. A miss is never a licence to slate, and never a licence to invent a punt costume.
props.verdictLabel: log the miss, do not slate
props.sparkLine: A miss is a design card. Not a slate.

beats.narration_text: The verdict. The nopunt skill is the anti dash punt catalog — the single place a Brutalist author checks before dropping any placeholder. HOLD is only a genuine archival photograph. Everything else in the catalog animates, so unfilled means bug. Step zero is the library — art scenes, then art scenes dash dash check. Narration shape picks the tool — Manim for moving math, Remotion for composed cards, the app skin for real code, FormB for lists, FormA for last resort words. SHOW slash HOLD slash CARD is the vocabulary. Anything else is a PUNT. And a genuine miss is a design card, never a slate.

props.artifactHeading: The catalog. The vocabulary. The block-list.
artifactLines: One file — skills/make/nopunt/SKILL.md — is the single source; sibling skills reference it, never repeat it.
HOLD is ONLY a genuine archival photograph. Everything else in the catalog animates — unfilled = PUNT (bug).
Step zero is the library — ./art scenes '<needs>' and ./art scenes --check <Name>. A hit is a lead; open the file.
Narration shape picks the tool: Manim (moving math), Remotion (cards/UI), app skin (real code), FormB (lists), FormA (last-resort words).

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer with a paste-ready audit prompt. Liam reads aloud + discusses. Safe: audits, never rewrites.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code. Read skills slash make slash nopunt slash SKILL dot md. Pick one delivered reel of your own — one you have already shipped, so nothing is at risk. Open its beat sheet dot json and classify every beat as SHOW, HOLD, or CARD, using the rule from section SHOW slash HOLD slash CARD. For any beat that does not fit those three, quote its narration text back and route it to a catalog row. And check three things at the sheet level. Is there a FRAMEWORK beat before the first worked example. Is there a FALSIFIABILITY beat that stress dash tests the framework. Does the YOUR TURN prompt in the sheet carry a rubric — a check the viewer can score. If any answer is no, name the fix. Do not rewrite. Just find the punts.
